open_points.subject: _write_service_answer
open_points.text: _write_service_answer: [RETURN_SHAPE] MUST answer, for a RefusedAnswer, an HttpResponse whose status is the status of the row of the refusal's code in the imported REFUSAL_HTTP_STATUSES constant and whose body is one JSON object encoded by the imported TEXT_ENCODING constant of exactly code, stage and failures: the code's value, the stage as a JSON number or JSON null when it is None, and each failure in its order as an object of its kind's value and its path, a JSON array of its elements, each element written as the one value it holds, its name as a JSON string or else its position as a JSON number, never as an object or JSON null; and for every other variant of = models.OperationAnswer, an HttpResponse whose status is the imported SERVICE_ANSWER_STATUS constant and whose body is one JSON object encoded by the imported TEXT_ENCODING constant of the variant's own fields without answer_kind, each nested model written as an object of its fields without view_kind; for a ValidationAnswer and a ContextAnswer the body MUST be the nested view alone, not wrapped in its field.
open_points.other_text: - PathElement fields (exact, no others exist): name: str | None, position: int | None
open_points.question: Must PathElement guarantee exactly one non-None field, or must serialization define behavior for elements whose fields are both None or both non-None?
